design_principles: Effort-tiered batching: lightest items first for early wins and momentum
Risk severity balanced within each batch for consistent throughput
Topic grouping within batches for pedagogically consistent distractor authoring
Governance-guard Rule 5: maximum 28 items per batch
Pack C and Pack D can execute in parallel (different source files)
Independent post-batch verification required after each batch
CorrectChoice lock required before Batch A begins (Pre-Flight §1)

CC AUDIT — Verify all 38 seeds have authoritative CC values via boundary-aware object extraction
BACKUP — Create timestamped backups of pack_c_corrected.js and pack_d_corrected.js
GOVERNANCE — Run governance-guard test suite, confirm 0 FAIL

batches.name: Complex Remediation — DL-013 Boilerplate + DL-010 Misalignment + Weak EC
batches.primary_work: Replace 8 DL-013 boilerplate EW slots with genuine choice-specific distractor explanations. Fix 2 DL-010 misaligned EW slots (EC-020: EWB, EWC). Fill 6 remaining empty non-CC EW slots. Rewrite 3 critically weak ECs (EC-014: fraud triangle, ED-036: change management, ED-075: segregation approval/reconciliation). Enrich 4 marginal ECs.

P1-EC-014.issue: 2 empty EW (A, B per cert results), EC is bare definition (150 chars, score 4/10). Fraud triangle is a foundational concept.
P1-EC-014.remediation: Fill both empty EW slots. Substantially rewrite EC — add ACFE/COSO P8 citation, business interpretation (Oakhurst scenario), fraud detection implications, exam-trap guidance on distinguishing fraud triangle from COSO ERM framework.

P1-EC-020.issue: DL-010 CRITICAL. EWB and EWC describe physical access controls from a different question (not the Emberton vendor-setup/payment scenario). EWD is empty. All 3 distractor slots are broken — zero usable learner feedback. This is the single highest-priority DL-010 item in the audit.
P1-EC-020.remediation: Full re-authoring of all 3 distractor EW slots to match the Emberton physical-control-over-assets stem (locked warehouse, badge access). EC needs minor COSO control-activity mapping addition.

P1-ED-016.issue: 1 empty EW (A). EWB and EWC are classic DL-013 boilerplate 'This option reflects a misunderstanding of erm risk response strategies...' EC is brief (152 chars, score 5/10) — no business interpretation, no COSO ERM citation.
P1-ED-016.remediation: Replace EWB and EWC with genuine choice-specific distractor explanations (distinguish risk avoidance, acceptance, mitigation, transfer). Fill EW_A. Enrich EC with COSO ERM (2017) citation, risk response taxonomy, Quintwood business-context interpretation.

P1-ED-036.issue: 1 empty EW (A). EWB and EWC are DL-013 boilerplate. EC is the weakest in the entire audit (144 chars, score 3/10) — bare statement 'Change management controls... are a category of IT general controls.' No explanation of WHY testing/approval/documentation matter.
P1-ED-036.remediation: Replace EWB and EWC with genuine choice-specific explanations (distinguish change management from application controls, physical controls). Fill EW_A. Substantially rewrite EC — explain testing/approval/documentation lifecycle, business risk of unauthorized changes causing financial statement errors, COSO control-activity linkage.

P1-ED-046.issue: 2 empty EW (A, C). EWD is DL-013 boilerplate with truncated text ('effectiven'). EC is brief (158 chars, score 5/10) — definition-only, no COSO P1 reference.
P1-ED-046.remediation: Replace EWD with genuine choice-specific explanation. Fill EW_A and EW_C. Enrich EC with COSO P1 citation (integrity and ethical values), control environment linkage, code-of-conduct role in fraud prevention.

P1-ED-051.issue: 2 empty EW (A, D). EWB is DL-013 boilerplate with text-to-slot mismatch (references 'balanced scorecard metrics' but assigned to slot B about 'replace segregation of duties'). Additionally flagged as DL-010 (MEDIUM). EC is brief (167 chars, score 6/10).
P1-ED-051.remediation: Replace EWB with genuine explanation for 'replace segregation of duties' distractor. Fill EW_A and EW_D. Enrich EC with MFA vs. single-factor contrast, defense-in-depth concept, COSO ITGC linkage.

P1-ED-075.issue: 1 empty EW (A). EWB and EWD are DL-013 boilerplate. EC is brief (153 chars, score 4/10) — definition-only, no COSO reference. This is the single worst-covered item in the pool (all 3 distractor slots are either empty or boilerplate).
P1-ED-075.remediation: Replace EWB and EWD with genuine choice-specific explanations (distinguish approval-reconciliation separation from revenue recognition issues, cash discounts). Fill EW_A. Substantially rewrite EC — explain why separating approval from reconciliation provides independent check, identify specific errors it detects, Alderway scenario application.

estimated_session_time: 5-7 hours (assuming 3-5 min per EW slot + 8-12 min per EC enrichment + 15-25 min per full EC rewrite + 15-25 min per DL-013/DL-010 replacement). Parallel Pack C/D sub-batches reduce wall-clock time. Independent verification adds ~15-20 min per batch.
critical_path: Batch C → EC-020 (DL-010 full re-authoring) is the riskiest single item. Batch A is the largest (19 items) and longest in wall-clock time despite lowest per-item effort.
parallel_opportunities: Within every batch, Pack C and Pack D sub-batches can execute in parallel (different pack files). Batch A: 13 Pack C items (~80 min) || 6 Pack D items (~35 min). Batch B: 4 Pack C items (~30 min) || 8 Pack D items (~60 min). Batch C: 2 Pack C items (~40 min) || 5 Pack D items (~90 min).

2. BATCH A PACK C + PACK D (parallel): 19 items, 24 writes
3. INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION: Spot-check 5+ items across both packs
4. BATCH B PACK C + PACK D (parallel): 12 items, 32 writes
5. INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION: Spot-check 5+ items, confirm 0 DL-026 regression
6. BATCH C PACK C + PACK D (parallel): 7 items, 27 writes

notes: This plan is a re-optimization of Agent H's 4-wave/7-sub-batch plan. Agent H's topic grouping was retained as the organizational principle within each effort-tiered batch, preserving the COSO framework → Control Activities → IT Controls → Capstone conceptual progression.
Batch A has 19 items (largest batch) — all are 1-EW-slot items with minimal per-item effort. Governance Rule 5 (≤28) is satisfied.
Batch C has only 7 items but comparable write volume (~27) to Batch A (~24) due to boilerplate replacements and EC rewrites requiring more complex authoring per slot.

The 5 cross-agent CC discrepancies (Agent C vs. Agent D) documented in AGENT_B_DEFECT_MANIFEST.json must be resolved before any write operations. The CC value determines which slot is CorrectChoice and therefore which EW slots are distractor slots requiring content.
EC-020 (DL-010 CRITICAL) is the single most urgent item — all 3 distractor slots provide wrong-topic or no feedback to learners. It should be tackled first within Batch C.
Metadata recalibration (DL-031 difficulty inflation, CognitiveLevel alignment, Difficulty label/score resolution) is deferred to a separate pass (S810.2) to keep S810.1 focused on content authoring.
